covers: rmodels.c's glTF materials as 6.2's LoadGLTF reads them, on a model made for it (makematerials.py): each material's twelve maps, their colors, values and textures (size, mipmaps, format and pixels), the base color factor's bytes, the metallic-roughness image split into grayscale roughness and metalness maps, those factors (raylib's only with it, helix-raylib's always: DECISIONS 71), the normal, occlusion and emissive textures and the emissive color only with its texture, nothing read without a pbrMetallicRoughness block
notes: The model's textures are RGBA PNGs and the metallic-roughness image an RGB one: helix-raylib's textures of a file's images say PIXELFORMAT_UNCOMPRESSED_R8G8B8A8 whatever the file's channels, where raylib's say the file's. The images are decoded by shared/PngDecoder.hx, as Node has no decoder; raylib's by stb_image. Material 2 ("factors") has factors and no metallic-roughness image: raylib's roughness and metalness values are 0, helix-raylib's the file's 0.15 and 0.45 (DECISIONS 71), so its value section's bar is 0.45; its colors and textures match exactly.
